real_estate.homebuilder: More than half of homes listed in our five cities carry HOA dues, and the median here is nearly three times the national figure.
real_estate.commentary:
Today's topic is the bill that is not in the list price: HOA dues. In Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 57% of listed homes carry them, against 44% nationally and 39% statewide, per Realtor.com. The median here is $395 a month, nearly three times the national $135; condos run $550, townhomes $380.

Compared with last October, the typical condo's dues are up only about 2%, to $560 in Fremont, Hayward, Newark and Union City, but two in three listed condos now ask $500 or more, up from 56%. More single family homes come with an HOA too: one in four, up from one in five.

Falling behind is getting costlier. Cotality counts 19,504 HOA liens in California in 2025, up 69.5% since 2022, and 3,404 HOA foreclosure filings; nationwide, filings rose 46% (the newsletter rounded it to 50%).

What this means for you: with Mortgage News Daily's 30-year at 7.57% Friday, every $100 of monthly dues costs a buyer about $14,200 of borrowing power, so a $550 condo fee is worth about $78,100. Buyers should read the budget and reserve study before offering; in California a board can raise regular dues up to 20% a year, and levy special assessments up to 5% of the budget, without a member vote. Sellers should have those documents ready on day one.

Locally, the five city ledger held at 664 and the board wide table eased to 2,687 from 2,700.

• Board wide: 2,687 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 168 coming soon and 215 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 664 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 585 are on the market and 79 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 240 live, 185 active, 32 coming soon, 22 brand new and 1 back on market. The median on market list price is $1,249,995 at $781 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 30 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 174, Milpitas 106, Newark 87, Union City 57.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,074,950 at $675 a square foot. 276 homes are priced under a million, and 132 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

All five cities: townhomes $380, single family homes with an HOA $161, all homes with dues $395. United States, 2025: all homes with dues $135. Right: the borrowing power dues cost at a 7.57% 30-year rate: $200 a month equals $28,400 of loan, $400 equals $56,800, $550 (the median condo) equals $78,100, and $700 equals $99,400.
